title: Web and Digital Interface Designers
description: Design digital user interfaces or websites. Develop and test layouts, interfaces, functionality, and navigation menus to ensure compatibility and usability across browsers or devices. May use web framework applications as well as client-side code and processes. May evaluate web design following web and accessibility standards, and may analyze web use metrics and optimize websites for marketability and search engine ranking. May design and test interfaces that facilitate the human-computer interaction and maximize the usability of digital devices, websites, and software with a focus on aesthetics and design. May create graphics used in websites and manage website content and links.

tasks.text: Create searchable indices for Web page content.
Design, build, or maintain Web sites, using authoring or scripting languages, content creation tools, management tools, and digital media.
Develop system interaction or sequence diagrams.
Develop Web site maps, application models, image templates, or page templates that meet project goals, user needs, or industry standards.
Direct and execute pre-production activities, such as creating moodboards or storyboards and establishing a project timeline.
Select programming languages, design tools, or applications.
Write supporting code for Web applications or Web sites.

clusters.label: Drafting, Laying Out, and Specifying Technical Devices, Parts, and Equipment

tasks.text: Create Web models or prototypes that include physical, interface, logical, or data models.
Develop and document style guidelines for Web site content.
Develop or implement procedures for ongoing Web site revision.
Incorporate technical considerations into Web site design plans, such as budgets, equipment, performance requirements, or legal issues including accessibility and privacy.

Provide clear, detailed descriptions of Web site specifications, such as product features, activities, software, communication protocols, programming languages, and operating systems software and hardware.
Identify or maintain links to and from other Web sites and check links to ensure proper functioning.
Identify problems uncovered by testing or customer feedback, and correct problems or refer problems to appropriate personnel for correction.
Perform or direct Web site updates.
Register Web sites with search engines to increase Web site traffic.
Conduct user research to determine design requirements and analyze user feedback to improve design quality.
Research and apply innovative solutions for product design, visuals, and user experience to meet the needs of individual Web development projects.
Research, document, rate, or select alternatives for Web architecture or technologies.

clusters.label: Communicating with Supervisors, Peers, or Subordinates

tasks.text: Collaborate with management or users to develop e-commerce strategies and to integrate these strategies with Web sites.
Collaborate with web development professionals, such as front-end or back-end developers, to complete the full scope of Web development projects.

clusters.label: Coordinating the Work and Activities of Others

tasks.text: Communicate with network personnel or Web site hosting agencies to address hardware or software issues affecting Web sites.
Confer with management or development teams to prioritize needs, resolve conflicts, develop content criteria, or choose solutions.
Develop, validate, and document test routines and schedules to ensure that test cases mimic external interfaces and address all browser and device types.
Perform Web site tests according to planned schedules, or after any Web site or product revision.
Document technical factors such as server load, bandwidth, database performance, and browser and device types.
Write and edit technical documentation for digital interface products and designs, such as user manuals, testing protocols, and reports.
Develop new visual design concepts and modify concepts based on stakeholder feedback.
Maintain understanding of current Web technologies or programming practices through continuing education, reading, or participation in professional conferences, workshops, or groups.
Respond to user email inquiries, or set up automated systems to send responses.

skills.name: Web platform development software
skills.def: Software to create or maintain applications accessed through web sites or using web technologies such as HTML. Examples: Adobe Flex, AJAX, Apache Struts, Apache Tomcat.

skills.name: Graphics or photo imaging software
skills.def: Software to draw or manipulate images. May adjust colors, add text, or apply special effects. Examples: Adobe Creative Cloud software, Adobe Illustrator, Adobe Photoshop, Adobe XD.

skills.name: Object or component oriented development software
skills.def: Software to create or maintain applications using object-oriented programming concepts. Examples: Advanced business application programming ABAP, Apache Groovy, Apache Spark, Apple Cocoa.

skills.name: Content workflow software
skills.def: Software to create, manage, or optimize content creation processes. May include collaboration or scheduling features. Examples: Atlassian JIRA, Sitecore CMS.

skills.name: Graphical user interface development software
skills.def: Software to create or maintain applications which interact with users through a graphical interface. Examples: Figma, Salesforce Visualforce.

skills.name: Development environment software
skills.def: Software to create or maintain applications which run on a computer or mobile device. Examples: Adobe ActionScript, Apache Ant, Apache Kafka, Apache Maven.
